biomarkers.name: HPV / p16
biomarkers.prevalence: Present in a subset of sinonasal SCC, especially non-keratinizing tumors; p16 is an imperfect surrogate and prevalence varies by series
biomarkers.clinical_use: HPV-associated multiphenotypic sinonasal carcinoma is a distinct entity, but in sinonasal SCC HPV-status is mainly diagnostically relevant in subsets and its prognostic advantage is less established than in oropharyngeal SCC

biomarkers.name: TP53
biomarkers.prevalence: Common, particularly in HPV-negative sinonasal SCC
biomarkers.clinical_use: Common tumor suppressor alteration; not a routinely used standalone clinical prognostic biomarker

biomarkers.name: SMARCB1 (INI-1)
biomarkers.prevalence: Subset (SMARCB1-deficient sinonasal carcinoma is a distinct entity)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Loss of INI-1 defines a distinct aggressive sinonasal carcinoma subtype

biomarkers.name: EGFR
biomarkers.prevalence: Recurrent exon 20 insertion mutations reported in a substantial subset of inverted papilloma-associated sinonasal SCC
biomarkers.clinical_use: Supports the molecular relationship of inverted papilloma and associated sinonasal SCC; hallmark driver in the inverted papilloma-associated subset

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Keratinizing SCC most common; also non-keratinizing

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Sinonasal epithelium (predominantly maxillary sinus and nasal cavity)
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: SMARCB1-deficient sinonasal carcinoma represents a distinct SWI/SNF-driven entity with undifferentiated/basaloid morphology
